cases.title: Bell-state preparation: the first entangled target
cases.semanticTier: exact finite matrix certificate + exact typed primitive circuit
cases.problem: Starting from |00>, prepare the Bell state (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), so the case introduces entanglement rather than another one-qubit amplitude change.
cases.contract: Lean proves normalization, a full 4 by 4 unitary completion, and an exact typed primitive route RY(pi/2) followed by CX whose zero-input action is the Bell state. The resource tuple (2,2,0,0) is computed from that same circuit. H followed by CX is an equivalent textbook witness, not the proof-bearing circuit scored here.

controlled-X that maps the |01> branch to |11>

cases.title: Dense real-amplitude preparation: a Möttönen-style two-qubit benchmark
cases.semanticTier: exact dense target + exact typed root-RY/UCRY circuit
cases.problem: Prepare the genuinely dense non-product real state with amplitudes (39,52,60,144)/169 and expose the recursive uniformly-controlled-rotation architecture used by dense state synthesis.
cases.contract: The target is an exact nested-Pythagorean instance: the root split uses 5/13 and 12/13, while the two conditional branches use 3/5,4/5 and 5/13,12/13. Lean proves target normalization, a full unitary completion, the exact typed root-RY plus one-control-UCRY state action, and circuit-derived cost (5,4,0,0).

cases.title: Structured probability loading: product structure beats the generic tree
cases.semanticTier: two exact typed circuits + same-target resource theorem
cases.problem: Prepare amplitudes (9,12,12,16)/25, whose probabilities come from two identical Bernoulli factors. Compare the generic recursive tree with the circuit obtained by exposing product structure.
cases.contract: Lean proves both typed primitive circuits prepare the same exact target. The generic root-RY plus one-control-UCRY circuit has cost (5,4,0,0); the factorized circuit contains two independent RY gates, cost (2,1,0,0). A named betterThan theorem certifies strict lexicographic improvement.

cases.title: Sparse state preparation: prune the zero branches
cases.semanticTier: exact d=3 target + two exact typed same-target circuits
cases.problem: Prepare a three-qubit state with only d=3 nonzero amplitudes, (3|000>+4|010>+12|100>)/13, and make the savings from a known-zero amplitude layer explicit.
cases.contract: Lean proves exact normalization and a full 8 by 8 unitary completion. The pruned typed circuit uses a q2 root RY followed by a q2-controlled UCRY on q1 and has cost (5,4,0,0). The same-target dense baseline appends a two-control zero-angle UCRY on q0; Lean proves that appended block is exactly identity but its reference compiler still costs ten gates, yielding (15,13,0,0).
symbols: only d computational-basis amplitudes are nonzero
Li–Luo's exact preparation-unitary contract, specialized here to n=3,d=3
a semantic identity circuit that deliberately pays for the amplitude subtree known to be zero

cases.limitations: Fixed n=3,d=3 witness only. The asymptotic sparse constructions, ancilla tradeoffs, and Theorem 1 lower/upper bounds remain in Papers.

bell-state-preparation.readerGoal: Understand entanglement as an exact state-preparation contract carried by a concrete two-gate unitary circuit.
bell-state-preparation.whyThisCase: The Bell target cannot be represented as two independently prepared one-qubit states. The proof-bearing route creates one coherent branch bit and then correlates the second wire with it.
bell-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Small entangled resource states occur throughout teleportation, communication, phase-estimation subroutines, and error-correcting constructions.

source.queryExplanation: Eq. (1) and Sec. III provide the general state-vector/state-transformation contract. The Bell target and RY(pi/2)+CX witness are an ASPBE pedagogical specialization, not a circuit copied from the paper.

mottonen-dense-state-preparation.readerGoal: See how Möttönen's recursive UCRY architecture becomes a fully exact finite typed-circuit certificate.
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.whyThisCase: A dense non-product target has no sparse or tensor-product shortcut. The nested-Pythagorean amplitudes make every finite rotation exact while retaining the generic binary-tree structure.
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Dense amplitude loading is a front-end cost for many amplitude-encoded algorithms. Möttönen et al. supply a general UCRY state-synthesis architecture; ASPBE closes one exact two-qubit instantiation.

source.queryExplanation: The case is a finite instantiation of Eq. (6)–(8) and Fig. 3. The paper-wide arbitrary-n synthesis/count theorem is kept separate.

circuitReading: RY on q1 sets total branch masses 5/13 and 12/13.
One-control UCRY on q0 selects the 3/5,4/5 or 5/13,12/13 branch pair.

theorems.label: Finite paper benchmark
theorems.title: Möttönen Eq. (6)–(8)/Fig. 3 has an exact two-qubit typed instantiation
theorems.statementProse: Lean certifies normalization, a full unitary completion, the typed root-RY/UCRY state action, and cost (5,4,0,0).
proofSteps: The reference compiler equals its controlled block-diagonal specification.
The exact typed circuit prepares the target and supplies the resource tuple.

grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.readerGoal: Learn when structure in a probability distribution should remove conditional circuitry rather than merely alter angles.
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.whyThisCase: The four amplitudes factor into two identical one-qubit amplitude pairs. A generic binary tree is correct but needlessly conditional; the factorized route exposes two parallel rotations.
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Grover–Rudolph prepares states corresponding to efficiently integrable probability distributions. This finite product instance isolates the structural optimization while leaving the general integration/oracle machinery in Papers.

source.title: Creating superpositions that correspond to efficiently integrable probability distributions
source.queryExplanation: Eq. (1) gives the target probability-amplitude state; Eq. (3) and Eq. (6) give recursive refinement via controlled rotations.

circuitReading: Root RY followed by one-control UCRY gives a proof-bearing five-gate route.
Every amplitude is a product of 3/5 and 4/5.
The two RY gates touch different wires, so depth is one.
Both routes first prove the same state action, then betterThan compares costs.

theorems.label: Correctness theorem
theorems.title: Both typed circuits prepare the same exact product state
theorems.statementProse: Lean checks the exact target and proves state action for the generic tree and factorized circuit.
proofSteps: Two lifted RY matrices give the explicit product matrix.
Constant UCRY is exactly the same single-wire RY semantics.

improvement.title: Exploit product structure instead of paying for a conditional tree
improvement.statementProse: The factorized typed circuit uses two parallel rotations; the generic typed UCRY route uses five gates at depth four. The comparison theorem is downstream of exact state-action proofs.
proofSteps: Both routes prepare exactly the same amplitudes.
2<5 closes strict dominance already on gate count.

sparse-three-state-preparation.readerGoal: See sparsity as a missing amplitude subtree that can be removed from an exact typed circuit.
sparse-three-state-preparation.whyThisCase: Only basis indices 0,2,4 carry amplitude. A structure-blind amplitude tree can spend gates compiling a final q0 layer even though q0 is known to remain zero on all support points.
sparse-three-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Li–Luo studies sparse-state circuit complexity asymptotically. ASPBE starts with an exact n=3,d=3 witness of Eq. (2), then makes one finite pruning mechanism machine-checkable without claiming Theorem 1.

source.title: Nearly Optimal Circuit Size for Sparse Quantum State Preparation
source.queryExplanation: Eq. (1) describes d-sparse input data and Eq. (2) states the exact preparation-unitary contract. The asymptotic Theorem 1 remains a Papers reproduction frontier.

circuitReading: Only 0,2,4 are nonzero; q0 is zero on every supported basis state.
RY on q2 creates masses 5/13 and 12/13.
One-control UCRY on q1 produces 3/13 and 4/13; the q2=1 branch uses zero angle.
Append a two-control zero-angle UCRY on q0; Lean proves its exact matrix is identity.
Remove that identity subtree and compare the circuit-derived tuples.

theorems.label: Sparse finite theorem
theorems.title: The n=3,d=3 Li–Luo Eq. (2) witness has an exact typed preparation route
theorems.statementProse: Lean checks exact normalization, full-unitary completion, the pruned typed circuit state action, and the same-target dense baseline.
proofSteps: Use the 3-4-5 split on q1 when q2=0.
A two-control UCRY with every angle zero evaluates exactly to identity.
Both circuits therefore prepare the same target.

improvement.title: Prune the provably identity zero-amplitude layer
improvement.statementProse: The dense reference compiler spends ten extra gates on a two-control zero-angle UCRY whose semantics is exactly identity. Removing it preserves the state and strictly improves the resource tuple.
proofSteps: Both circuits are already exact state-preparation routes.
Pruned route plus the identity UCRY yields (15,13,0,0).
